newsitem.title: UK: IPE fines PVM, several floor team for rule breaches.
newsitem.headline: IPE fines PVM, several floor team for rule breaches.

text.p: The International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) said on Friday it had fined PVM Oil Futures Ltd and several of its trading floor staff of "certain breaches" of the exchange's regulations.

The IPE, the world's second largest energy futures exchange, said PVM was fined 30,000 stg after it "accepted liability" for the actions of several of its floor trading team which broke IPE rules between October 30, 1995 and March 28, 1996.
The exchange said "possible irregularities" were identified as "a result of routine continuous surveillance."
According to an IPE statement, Simon Jocham was fined 8,000 stg after he "admitted he had failed to execute an unmatched client order, contrary to the regulations."
Jocham also admitted "bringing the exchange into disrepute" was fined an additional 8,000 stg and suspended from entering the market for six months from December 16, 1996, the IPE said.
The IPE said Robert Evans "admitted that he withdrew from an executed cross trade" and was fined 2,500 stg while David Kavanagh also admitted to an unmatched cross trade and was fined 1,500 stg.
Mark Sangster was fined 1,100 stg for failing to execute an unmatched client cross trade.
All defendants are to meet their own costs as well as those of the exchange, the IPE said.
